neighbours.label: a physical object reaching or entering a changed state in a hands-on process: the pronoun or verb at the point where something is lit, dries, stops or inflates ('lit it', 'when it's dry', 'when it stops'); clerical actions on objects ('read it', 'filed it') stay low
fire: She took a candle from the drawer, held a match to the wick, and lit it.
Brush on the glue, and when it is dry, press the two boards together.
Step into the lift and get off when it stops at the lobby.
Pull the cord and the raft will inflate in about ten seconds.
He rolled a cigarette, put it between his lips, and lit it slowly.
Spread the plaster thin, and when it is dry, sand it smooth.
Wait on the platform and board the tram when it stops completely.
Twist the cap open and the sleeping pad will inflate by itself.
quiet: She took a notebook from the drawer, opened the cover, and signed it.
Write the letter carefully, and when it is done, mail it to the office.
Step into the lobby and sign in when you reach the front desk.
Pull the file and the clerk will review it in about ten minutes.
He picked up the report, put it on the desk, and initialed it slowly.
Fill out the form, and when it is complete, hand it to the nurse.
Wait at the counter and pay the cashier when your name is called.
Open the envelope and the invoice will explain the charges.

predictions: fire 0.35-0.95 on ' it' or the state verb; near misses below 0.15
short: object entering a physical state change
notes: Card: + pole peaks on ' it', ' to', ' take' (take fire), ' when', in lighting, drying, inflating and elevator contexts. Probe: 'struck it, and lit it' 0.976, 'when it's dry' 0.681, 'mattress will inflate' 0.606, 'when it stops' 0.469, 'take fire' 0.347, 'until it cools down' 0.272; 'read it, and filed it' 0.103, 'approved it' 0.005.
